The prompt says "At the end they must propose one complete (including typical use cases, edge cases, and error scenarios) JUnit 4 test file (SerializationUtilsTest.java)". So we should produce that file. It must start with ###Test START## and end with ###Test END##. Provide test cases covering methods: clone, serialize(Serializable, OutputStream), serialize(Serializable) returning byte[], deserialize(InputStream), deserialize(byte[]), also ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream behavior maybe indirectly. Include typical use cases, edge cases, error scenarios: null inputs, invalid streams, exception handling, verify deep clone works, verify that serialization and deserialization produce equal objects but not same reference, test with custom class with nested objects, test that serialization of non-serializable object triggers SerializationException (but method signature only accepts Serializable, compile-time prevents non-serializable; but we could pass a serializable that throws exception in writeObject?). Could create a class that implements Serializable but throws IOException in writeObject to cause exception. Also test that ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream resolves class using thread context classloader if provided classloader can't find class.

We need to import JUnit 4 (org.junit.Test, org.junit.Assert). Use expected exceptions via @Test(expected=...). Use try/catch for verifying thrown exceptions with messages.

Also test that serialize throws IllegalArgumentException when outputStream null, deserialize throws IllegalArgumentException when inputStream null, and deserialize(byte[]) null.

Test that close of streams is handled: after serialize, outputStream closed? Actually ObjectOutputStream close will close underlying stream; we can use ByteArrayOutputStream which can be used after close; but we can test that close does not throw.

Test that clone returns null when input null.

Test deep clone: create mutable object (e.g., a HashMap) and ensure modifications after clone don't affect original.

Test that ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream fallback works: create a custom class loader that cannot load the class (returns null) and ensure deserialization still works due to fallback to thread context classloader. This is tricky but we can simulate by using a custom classloader that throws ClassNotFoundException for that class name, then set thread context loader to original classloader. Provide custom class that is serializable. Then use SerializationUtils.clone with that class loader? In clone, they pass object's classloader to ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream. If that loader cannot find class, fallback uses context classloader (which is default). So test that cloning works even if object's classloader can't load class. We'll create a simple custom classloader that overrides loadClass to delegate to parent for all except the test class name, and for that name, throws ClassNotFoundException. Then set thread context classloader to original. Then call clone. It should still succeed.

Also test that ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream resolves class correctly when classloader can load.
